# Computational support with independent output queries {#sec-computational-support}

**Giving ISLA a problem-derived computational support and decoding the
requested interior points passively from it, at the same depth and with the
same inputs as the interacting configuration, loses 43% on interior pressure,
34% on velocity and 140% on eddy viscosity. The accuracy of ISLA's interior
configuration is inseparable from letting the requested queries interact.**
This closes the audit's first direction as proposed, and it says what the
interacting queries are doing: they are not a convenience of batching but the
computation itself.

## The question and why it mattered {#sec-computational-support-question}

ISLA's interior configuration ("query tokens + SDF") joins the requested
interior points to the encoder as interacting tokens carrying their signed
distance to the surface and its gradient. It led GeoTransolver-volume on
velocity and, in bf16, on pressure. Its defect for deployment is that the
prediction at a point depends on which other points are requested with it
(pressure 0.062 at 10,000 queries, 0.077 at 2,000, 0.110 at 1,000 on fixed
sentinel points in the program book's measurements). The audit's reading was
that the queries supply a rich, geometry-aware computational state, and that
letting the caller's query set define that state is an avoidable choice: derive
a support set from the problem instead, let it interact, and read the requested
points off the resulting state passively. Anchored UPT is the precedent. The
preregistration (`studies/computational_support/PREREG.md`) fixed the arms and
the bars before any lane ran.

## What was built {#sec-computational-support-built}

`ISLA(support_tokens=True, query_independent=True, n_query_scalars=1,
query_mass="source_total", n_decoder_layers=K)`: the support points are
interacting tokens with the same invariant seeds as the surface tokens (a
token-type offset, the signed distance as a scalar, its gradient as the token
normal) and a learned total mass equal to a learned fraction of the total
source measure, so the measure-scale and source-refinement contracts hold; the
requested points are passive queries decoded through K read blocks that see the
final slice states, the anchors and a measure-normalized log-space kernel
readout of all encoder tokens. Ten contract tests cover exact query
independence with the support fixed, SE(3) covariance, drive degree one,
measure-scale and refinement invariance, gauge scale equivariance and gradient
flow. The recipe transform `SplitInteriorSupport` moves the first 5,000 points
of the reader's deterministic 10,000-point per-case sample into the support set
with their signed distance and gradient; the remaining 5,000 are scored. That
split was verified on the saved artifacts: the scored points are exactly the
second half of the reference arm's 10,000-point sample for every car checked,
so the per-point relative errors are comparable.

## Readout {#sec-computational-support-readout}

Frozen V0 protocol on DrivAerML volume (435 training cars, 500 epochs, lr
1e-3, bf16 training, 10,000 surface cells and 10,000 interior points), two
seeds per arm, float32 inference, same-snapshot references (the interacting
reference re-evaluated under the study's code snapshot reproduces its recorded
values to the digit, @sec-nb-evalpoints-verdict).

``` {.python .cell-code}
import json
from pathlib import Path
d = json.loads(Path("studies/computational_support/d1_verdict_2026-09-10.json").read_text())
A = d["per_arm"]
rows = [("(i) reference: query tokens + SDF, 10,000 interacting queries", "isla_qtsdfval"),
        ("(ii) SUPPORT-12: 5,000 interacting support + 5,000 passive queries, 12 read blocks", "isla_support12"),
        ("(iii) SUPPORT-4: same, 4 read blocks", "isla_support4"),
        ("(iv) PASSIVE-12: no support, 5,000 passive queries, 12 read blocks", "isla_passive12"),
        ("GeoTransolver-volume, unit drive, for scale", "udrv_gt_vol")]
print("| arm | seeds | pressure | velocity | eddy viscosity |")
print("|---|---|---|---|---|")
for n, k in rows:
    m = A[k]["mean"]; s = A[k]["per_seed"]
    print(f"| {n} | {len(A[k]['seeds'])} | {m['pressure_l2']:.4f} | {m['velocity_l2']:.4f} | {m['nut_l2']:.4f} |")
print()
b = d["verdict"]["d1"]["bars_at_reference"]
print(f": Interior relative L2 on the 48 DrivAerML validation cars, float32, two-seed means. Preregistered bars at the float32 reference: supported if SUPPORT-12 ≤ {b['supported_max']['pressure_l2']:.4f} / {b['supported_max']['velocity_l2']:.4f} / {b['supported_max']['nut_l2']:.4f}; falsified if pressure ≥ {b['falsified_pressure_min']:.4f}. Data: studies/computational_support/d1_verdict_2026-09-10.json. {{#tbl-d1}}")
```

**Verdict: falsified.** SUPPORT-12 scores 0.078 on pressure against a
falsification bar of 0.060 (1.43x the reference), 0.107 on velocity (1.34x)
and 0.269 on eddy viscosity (2.41x); the two seeds agree to 2%. The
decomposition the preregistration asked for says how little each ingredient of
the passive route is worth: going from 4 to 12 read blocks buys 13% on pressure
(0.090 → 0.078), adding the 5,000-point interacting support buys 12% (0.089 →
0.078), and neither touches eddy viscosity, which is worse with the support
than without. Both together leave the passive route 43% behind the interacting
queries on pressure and 52% behind GeoTransolver-volume. The sentinel-query
study of the preregistration (query-set dependence of the passive path) was not
run: with the accuracy half falsified its outcome could not have changed the
verdict, and query independence of the passive path is already exact by
construction and by test.

Cost, for completeness: SUPPORT-12 trains at 0.71–0.75 s per step and 10.8 GB
against the reference's 0.28 s and 6.1 GB (the arms ran unpinned, a measured
+35% on this hardware, so the like-for-like factor is about 1.9x), SUPPORT-4 at
0.67–0.87 s and 7.1 GB, PASSIVE-12 at 0.62–0.63 s and 5.9 GB. The passive
route is slower as well as worse.

## What this says about the interacting queries {#sec-computational-support-reading}

The eddy-viscosity number is the diagnostic one. A support set of 5,000
interior points with signed distance and gradient is a rich, geometry-aware
state by any reasonable description, and the passive readout sees the final
slice states, the anchors and a kernel over every encoder token; yet its eddy
viscosity is 2.4x worse than when the requested points themselves interact.
What the interacting queries provide is therefore not context about the
geometry, which the support supplies as well, but computation at the requested
points: each query's representation is refined through the encoder layers by
attention with the other tokens, and a read block that only reads the finished
state cannot reproduce that. This is the alternative reading the audit flagged
(the accuracy is inseparable from letting the requested queries interact), and
it is the one the data support. Two consequences follow. The deployment repair
for the query-set dependence goes through training on varied query counts
(query-count augmentation, owned by the main program), not through
architecture. And the passive route at matched depth and inputs is closed for
ISLA in this program; what remains open on the interior is the far-field
deficit of the interacting configuration (@sec-campaigns-interior), which is a
different question.

directory, launcher `v0/v0_support_aga.sbatch`, code snapshot `code_support`),
evaluated in float32 under the program's evaluation snapshot with no skipped
loads; references `v0_isla_qtsdfval_seed{42,43}` re-evaluated under the same
snapshot. Reduction `studies/computational_support/grade_d1.py`; preregistration
`PREREG.md`; launch and ops record in the notebook from @sec-nb-d1-launch
onward, verdict at @sec-nb-d1-verdict.
